sentence: We present the case of a 21-year-old male patient, with no known allergies or other history, who came to the emergency room with a 6-month clinical picture of asthenia, increased fatigue with moderate exercise and accompanied by a general syndrome with weight loss in said months of about 10 kilos.

Due to episodes of abdominal pain during this period, he visited the Emergency Department on two occasions and underwent gastroscopy, which reported minimal hiatal hernia with grade I esophagitis and duodenal-gastric bile reflux.
In the last 5 days the symptoms worsened, also presenting vomiting, more intense diffuse abdominal pain and liquid stools without an increase in their number.

On physical examination, he had a blood pressure of 120/60 mmHg, heart rate of 110 pm, afebrile, conscious and oriented, without neurological focality, eupneic, cardiac auscultation was rhythmic, tachycardic, without murmurs, the abdomen was soft and depressible.
Diffusely painful, without defense to palpation, no masses or megalia are palpable.
The generalized skin hyperpigmentation stands out, accentuated in the nipples, genital area and with melanic spots on the palate and gingival edges.

The analysis upon admission shows a blood glucose of 59 mg/dL, creatinine 4.32 mg/dL, urea 214 mg/dL, Na 123 mg/dL, K 8.0 mg/dL, Ca 8.2 mg/dL, an arterial blood gas analysis with a pH of 7.24, pCO2 35.6 mmHg, pO2 107 mmHg (with O2 at 4 liters/minute), bicarbonate 14.4 mmol/L, EB - 11.3 mmol/L and SatO2 of 97, 2%.
The blood count shows a hemoglobin of 13.4 g/dl, hematocrit 39.5%, MCV 83 fL, leukocytes 12,800 (45% neutrophils, 32% lymphocytes, 12% monocytes and 10.5% eosinophils).
The electrocardiogram shows sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm with RSR' configuration and QT prolongation (487 ms).

During his stay in the emergency room, measures were initiated to correct the hyperkalemia, but the patient progressively became more sweaty, tachycardic, and hypotensive (BP 85/46 mmHg), so with suspicion of an Addisonian crisis, it was decided to admit him to the ICU. and volume replacement is started with saline solution (4,500 cc in the first 24 hours), provision of glucose,ctocortin (100 mg i.v. bolus followed by 400 mg in continuous intravenous infusion in the following 24 hours); initially requiring perfusion of vasopressor amines (dopamine at 10 mcg/kg/min), which can be withdrawn in 36 hours.
Blood samples taken prior to the start of corticosteroid treatment to determine adrenal function showed a basal cortisol of 4.0 mg/dL and a plasma ACTH of 264 pg/ml.
The determination of anti-adrenal capsule antibodies in serum by indirect immunofluorescence was positive with a titer of 1/80.
The determination of thyrotropin, free thyroxine, FSH and LH, as well as antithyroglobulin and antimicrosomal peroxidase antibodies were within normal ranges.
Abdominal CT: presence of morphologically normal adrenal glands.

The patient was discharged from the Intensive Care Unit 3 days after admission and from the hospital 7 days later with analytical parameters of renal function and ions within normal limits and with treatment with hydroaltresone 20 mg PO/8 h.
